scenes.text: An expense request passes through several hands. Omar submits it, Amina makes the decision, background processing prepares the outcome, and another system receives it. If those handoffs live in separate tools, a delay or failure becomes difficult to trace and explain.

scenes.text: QueueForge keeps those handoffs connected on one record. It is not chat or a general project tracker. It controls approval, background processing, delivery, and the history people need to inspect.
captions: QueueForge keeps those handoffs connected on one record.

scenes.text: The work is divided among three roles. Omar, the operator, starts requests. Amina, the approver, makes the independent decision. An administrator configures the workspace and watches its health. After sign-in, each person sees only the pages and actions their role allows. Everything here uses local demonstration data.

scenes.text: Here is the workspace map. Home is the starting point, showing priorities, current status, and work that needs attention. Request types is where administrators build the forms, approval rules, processing steps, and delivery path that each request follows. Delivery connections shows where finished results go and whether they arrived. People and access controls who can enter and what each role may do. Processing health separates work that is waiting, running, retrying, or needs help. Activity log preserves important changes and lets administrators inspect the details. Notifications is each person's inbox for decisions, completed work, retries, and problems. Together, these seven pages follow one request from setup to proof.

scenes.text: Step one. Omar opens Start and track requests, chooses Expense review, and enters twelve hundred fifty dirhams. He selects cost center O P S forty-two and adds the summary, Dubai client workshop airfare, September twenty twenty-six. Before he sends it, the review page shows who will approve the request and what happens next. Omar submits, and QueueForge marks it Waiting for approval with the next person named.

scenes.text: Step two. Amina opens the Approval inbox and searches Dubai client workshop. Omar's request appears with the same details he submitted. She reviews them and approves. Omar cannot approve his own request, so QueueForge saves Amina's independent decision before processing begins.

scenes.text: Step three. QueueForge starts the background work. The first attempt fails, but it remains visible. QueueForge tries again, and the second attempt succeeds. It creates a signed receipt so the completed result can be verified, then delivers it. In Delivery connections, the administrator searches Expense review and finds the matching send. The delivery record confirms it was accepted, and Omar's request now reads Completed.
